shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures edged higher on Tuesday, supported by firmer Thai physical prices and signs of tight supply, even as weakness in top consumer China's auto sector weighed on market sentiment.($1 = 158.2900 yen)($1 = 6.6943 Chinese yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures edged higher on Tuesday, supported by firmer Thai physical prices and signs of tight supply, even as weakness in top consumer China's auto sector weighed on market sentiment.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for March delivery
was up 3.1 yen, or 0.67%, at 462.9 yen ($2.92) per kg as of 0220 GMT. The market was closed on Monday for a holiday
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
fell 110 yuan, or 0.53%, to 20,670 yuan ($3,087.70) per metric ton
The most-active November butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) slumped 415 yuan, or 2.5%, to 16,185 yuan per ton
Prices of Thailand's benchmark export-grade smoked rubber sheet (RSS3) (RUB-RSS3C-BKK) and block rubber (RUB-STR20C-BKK) were up 1.34% and 1.03%, respectively
Short-term natural rubber warehouse receipts remain low, far below levels in previous years, analysts from broker Guangzhou Futures said in a note
Rubber inventories in warehouses monitored by the Shanghai Futures Exchange fell 0.2% from the last release on September 30, the exchange said on Friday
Malaysia's natural rubber exports fell 18.2% month-on-month to 33,426 tons in August, even as production rose 9.6% to 29,510 tons, data from the Department of Statistics Malaysia showed on Monday
China's passenger vehicle sales fell 28.1% year-on-year to 1.63 million units in September, after a 23.7% decline in August, data from the China Passenger Car Association showed on Monday
Automobile sales could influence the pace of automobile manufacturing, which involves using rubber-made tyres
The European Union and China reached a deal to limit Chinese hybrid car imports to 350,000 vehicles a year, with measures to take effect from early December, an EU Commission official said on Monday
The curbs add to pressure on Chinese automakers already facing slowing domestic sales
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for January delivery (STFF7) last traded at 262 U.S. cents per kg, up 0.3%
